references.text: Jacob's sons react with anger because Shechem had committed a shameful act in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter.
Simeon and Levi avenge their sister Dinah's dishonor by killing all the men in Shechem's city.
The provisions of the Mosaic law regarding rape of a virgin, which may relate to Shechem's action against Dinah.
A parallel account of sexual violence - the concubine at Gibeah was abused throughout the night.
The Benjamites recount the sexual violence in Gibeah, a parallel to Shechem's action.
Amnon's rape of Tamar - the closest parallel to Shechem's action against Dinah in the Old Testament, with similar language about dishonor.
Direct continuation of the same event; shows how the violence escalates into political negotiation.
Shows the consequence of the violation: how the violence leads to a broader conspiracy.
A linguistic and thematic parallel that underscores the pattern of sexual violence in patriarchal structures.
Shows how the violation escalates into a collective moral and theological downfall for the entire city.
Direct narrative connection; shows the attempt to legitimize violence through public speech.
